record.original_question: If two Artin groups of spherical type are quasi-isometric, must they be commensurable? (This is not true for right-angled Artin groups.)

evidence.quote: If two Artin groups of spherical type are quasi-isometric, must they be commensurable? (This is not true for right-angled Artin groups.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a finite set and let $M=(m_{st})_{s,t\in S}$ be a Coxeter matrix, i.e. $m_{ss}=1$ and $m_{st}=m_{ts}\in\{2,3,4,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ for $s\neq t$. The associated Artin group is
$$A_M=\langle\, S \mid \underbrace{sts\cdots}_{m_{st}\text{ factors}}=\underbrace{tst\cdots}_{m_{st}\text{ factors}} \text{ for all } s\neq t \text{ with } m_{st}<\infty\,\rangle.$$
The Artin group $A_M$ is said to be of spherical (finite) type if the corresponding Coxeter group (obtained by adjoining the relations $s^2=1$ for all $s\in S$) is finite.

Two finitely generated groups $G_1,G_2$ (each equipped with a word metric for some finite generating set) are quasi-isometric if there exist a map $f\colon G_1\to G_2$ and constants $K\geq 1$, $C\geq 0$ such that
$$\tfrac{1}{K}d(x,y)-C\leq d(f(x),f(y))\leq K\,d(x,y)+C \quad \text{for all } x,y\in G_1,$$
and every point of $G_2$ lies within distance $C$ of the image of $f$. Two groups $G_1,G_2$ are commensurable if they contain finite-index subgroups $H_i\leq G_i$ with $H_1\cong H_2$.

Question: If two Artin groups of spherical type are quasi-isometric, must they be commensurable?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has established the commensurability classification among irreducible spherical Artin groups (e.g., showing Artin groups of types F₄ and H₄ are not commensurable with type D₄), but the quasi-isometric classification of spherical Artin groups remains incomplete, and no published proof asserts that QI implies commensurability for all spherical Artin groups. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Commensurability in Artin groups of spherical type
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the commensurability classification of irreducible spherical Artin groups; addresses several but not all cases.
status_evidence.claim: Commensurability classification of spherical Artin groups has been advanced but not fully completed; QI classification not addressed in full.

status_evidence.title: Artin groups of types F4 and H4 are not commensurable with that of type D4
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves outstanding commensurability cases among spherical Artin groups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent papers continue to resolve commensurability questions among spherical Artin groups, indicating the QI-vs-commensurability question remains active.
